GOAL! Sabah 0-2 Barcelona (Gordon, 51 mins)
A second goal for Barcelona and a second for Anthony Gordon! It’s a straightforward finish, after Stas Pokatilov in the home goal shovelled the ball right to his feet in saving Jesus’s shot.
⚽️ Updates from Wednesday’s 8pm GMT matches
 
⚽️ Live scoreboard | Read Football Daily | Email Simon
 Updated 
Key events
Team news is dripping through like glacial meltwater in early spring. Here’s how they line up at the Jan Breydelstadion:
Club Brugge v Liverpool
  
Club Brugge: Sommer, Sabbe, Spileers, Mechele, Seys, Potts, Vanaken, Forbs, Vetlesen, Lemarechal, Tresoldi. Subs: Jackers, Driessche, Lee, Virgili, Tsawa, Vermant, Dams, Robberechts, Siquet, Audoor, Diakhon, Vasovic.
 
Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, Araujo, Kerkez, Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Munoz, Wirtz, Barcola, Isak. Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, van Dijk, Mac Allister, Tsimikas, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha, Danns.
 
Referee: Alejandro Hernandez (Spain).
It’s half-time in the early games, with Anthony Gordon the author of the only goal scored so far. The scores, then:
Sabah 0-1 Barcelona
 
Slavia Prague 0-0 Villarreal
Hello world! Well I for one enjoyed Andoni Iraola’s pre-match briefing yesterday, in which he gushed over the team Liverpool will be playing this evening. “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them,” the Spaniard said of Club Brugge. “Sometimes you have to analyse a team and watch a lot of games and it’s a little boring but with Brugge that definitely doesn’t happen. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic. Everyone runs and they are very aggressive in the press.”
And a ludicrously superficial analysis demonstrates why they’ve been a fun side to check out: they haven’t failed to score in any game in any competition since 4 September, and in 12 fixtures since then their opponents have also scored in all but three. In their last five games, one in the Champions League and the rest in the good old Jupiler Pro, they’ve scored one once, two once, three once, four once and five once, winning four and drawing one, while their opponents have scored seven.
With Liverpool themselves in decent form (we won’t mention their 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in their last European outing) this looks a fun fixture and will be my main focus, though I’ll be keeping my beady eye on events elsewhere. At this point you may wish to know what games we’ve got ahead of us, so here they are: two Spanish sides visit teams whose name begin with S in the early kick-offs, with seven more Champions League ties to follow.
Kicking off at 5.45pm GMT:
 
Sabah v Barcelona
 
Slavia Prague v Villarreal
Kicking off at 8pm GMT:
 
Atletico Madrid v Viking
 
Club Brugge v Liverpool
 
Internazionale v Stuttgart
 
Lille v Bayern Munich
 
PSG v Roma
 
Shakhtar Donetsk v Fenerbahce (at Stamford Bridge)
 
Sporting v Man Utd
Also: Four Championship fixtures including the start of Edward Iordanescu’s Watford adventure, at home to Blackburn.
